learning_outcomes.text: That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that starts from the basis of general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts regarding the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solve engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Circulation of an electric field: electrical potential energy and electric potential.
Fundamental laws to calculate magnitudes in electric circuits
Force produced by a magnetic field
Point charge movement under the effect of a magnetic field
Magnetic field due to point charges in movement
Propagation of electromagnetic waves in dielectric and conductive materials
teaching_methods: Individual work, problem solving, and lab reports
assessment_rules: Passing requires completing all lab practices and exams, and achieving a minimum total of 5 points from the sum of partial exams (if passed and liberated), the final exam, and lab practices. Partial exams can be 'liberated' (passed and excluded from the final exam re-evaluation) if a score of 5/10 or higher is achieved. Students passing all three exams (Electricity, Waves, Magnetism+OEM) in the first call will have their exam score multiplied by 1.1. For the extraordinary call, scores from liberated partial exams and practices are retained, but approved parts are not carried over to subsequent academic years.
